## What's new

Threadnote 5.4.1 makes background code-graph embedding converge on busy repositories, speeds up GPU embedding, and keeps pull request watches alive and able to act when they wake.

### Faster, converging code-graph embedding

Background embedding now reuses vectors from in-progress generations, so a repository that refreshes often no longer starts embedding again from near zero on each snapshot. Abandoned in-progress generations are retired instead of accumulating.

Foreground embedding on a GPU-offloaded model, such as `embeddinggemma` on Metal, now uses up to four contexts instead of one. If the GPU has no memory for another context, Threadnote keeps the contexts it already has.

### Reliable pull request watches

A pull request watch collector now survives a superseding development install and stops only when the watch completes or you stop it. A collector that is no longer alive now shows as exited instead of running.

A Claude Code turn that a watch wakes can now use the watch tool to relay and acknowledge its notice. If the host still denies the tool, the attempt fails with `host-permission-denied` and is not recorded as complete.

### Smoother development workflows

- A `standard` compact start no longer fails when a ready code graph does not index an affected path, such as a CI workflow or Markdown file. Those paths stay uncited.
- `workflow_task_start` retries a short admission-busy failure up to three times.
- You can pass the delivered-PR watch hint to the watch tool as it is.

### Context Brief and website

- Context Brief lexical recall now gets the shared 5-second read budget instead of two seconds, so large memory corpora no longer exhaust it early.
- The website again builds and shows release pages whose headline fits the social card.
